news.headline: SpaceX (SPCX) Joins Nasdaq-100 on Fast-Track Rules, Triggering Billions in Passive Buying
news.body: SpaceX officially joined the Nasdaq-100 before Tuesday's open, just 15 trading days after its June 12 IPO — the first test of Nasdaq's new fast-track inclusion rule for mega-cap listings. J.P. Morgan estimates the inclusion triggers approximately $4.3 billion in passive buying from QQQ alone, with total cross-index demand potentially reaching $22–27 billion. The impact is amplified by a tight public float of only 3–5% of shares outstanding, creating an acute supply-demand imbalance. Historical data on prior Nasdaq-100 additions shows an average first-day loss of 1.13%, but SPCX's unprecedented scale and investor interest could drive atypical price action.

news.headline: S&P 500 Futures Slip Tuesday as Asian Chip Selloff Resumes; Nasdaq Eyes Lower Open
news.body: S&P 500 futures slipped 0.25% in early Tuesday trading as fresh selling pressure returned overnight in Asian semiconductor stocks, with South Korea's Kospi plunging more than 7% and dragging global tech sentiment lower just one session after Wall Street's broad Monday rally. Polymarket traders assigned only a 17% probability that the S&P 500 would open higher on Tuesday, reflecting heightened caution around chips that have powered much of 2026's gains. Markets will also watch Tuesday's U.S. trade deficit data for clues on economic health, while SpaceX officially begins trading as a Nasdaq-100 constituent. The cautious tone comes despite Monday's record Dow close above 53,000 and a 1.12% Nasdaq advance.

news.headline: Dell (DELL) Surges 8%+ After Trump Publicly Urges 'Go Buy a Dell Computer' at White House
news.body: Dell Technologies shares jumped more than 8% on July 6 after President Trump told the nation to 'go out and buy a Dell computer' during an Oval Office ceremony marking the launch of 'Trump Accounts,' a new tax-advantaged investment program for American children. The endorsement came as Dell CEO Michael Dell and his wife Susan were present at the event, having pledged over $6 billion to seed the program. Shares touched an intraday high of $428.29 from a prior close of $394.32, with the leveraged GraniteShares 2x Long DELL ETF (DLLL) surging 17%. Critics raised conflict-of-interest concerns as Trump's own financial disclosures show he purchased at least $1 million in Dell stock in Q1 2026.

news.headline: Anthropic Signs $19B, 20-Year Data Center Lease With TeraWulf; WULF Spikes 16%+ Premarket
news.body: TeraWulf (WULF) signed a 20-year AI data center lease with Anthropic expected to generate approximately $19 billion in contracted revenue — a figure exceeding the company's entire ~$12 billion market cap. The 401-megawatt campus at TeraWulf's Justified Data site in Hawesville, Kentucky, will deliver initial capacity in H2 2027 with full operations by early 2028. Shares surged as much as 19% intraday before settling up ~5%, with peers IREN (+13%) and Cipher Digital (+8%) also rallying on read-through AI infrastructure demand. Separately, TeraWulf agreed to sell its 50.1% stake in a Texas joint venture to Fluidstack for ~$530 million, monetizing prior investment and redirecting capital to wholly owned projects.

news.headline: Goldman Sachs Hikes AMD Target to $640, Citing Agentic AI CPU Boom; Shares Rally 6.6%
news.body: Goldman Sachs dramatically raised its 12-month price target on Advanced Micro Devices to $640 from $450 on July 6, reiterating a Buy rating and citing surging demand for high-performance server CPUs driven by the rise of agentic AI workloads. AMD shares climbed 6.61% to close at $552.05 on the Nasdaq, extending a roughly 161% year-to-date advance. The bank anchored its thesis in AMD's data center segment, which posted 57% year-over-year revenue growth to $5.8 billion, and flagged AMD's upcoming 'Advancing AI 2026' event on July 23 as a key catalyst. Goldman also raised price targets on Qualcomm to $180 and Western Digital to $650 the same day, signaling a broad semiconductor sector reassessment.

news.headline: Shanghai Composite Slides 1.3% on July 7 as AI Chip Rotation Hits Mainland China
news.body: The Shanghai Composite fell 1.3% to 3,990 on July 7, breaking below the 4,000 level, as the region-wide semiconductor and AI stock rotation intensified following Samsung's mixed Q2 guidance and the Hormuz LNG attack. The SSE had closed at just 4,041 on July 6 after a marginal 0.06% decline driven by similar AI sector de-risking. Technology and semiconductor equipment names led losses on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges. The break below 4,000 is technically significant, as that level had served as a closely watched support floor for mainland equities through the second quarter.

news.headline: Qatari LNG Tanker Hit by Drone/Missile Near Strait of Hormuz, Reigniting Energy Risk
news.body: The Al Rekayyat, a laden LNG carrier owned by Qatar's state-backed Nakilat, was struck by a projectile near the Omani coast as it exited the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Tuesday, triggering an engine room fire. Iran's IRGC reportedly fired at least two missiles at commercial vessels on Monday night, testing the fragile US-Iran ceasefire. The attack reignited risk-off sentiment across Asian markets — Japanese and South Korean tech stocks sold off sharply as capital rotated away from high-beta sectors, while Brent crude rose toward $73/bbl. The incident directly pressured energy-import-dependent Asian economies and amplified the broader selloff in KOSPI and Nikkei.

news.headline: Samsung Q2 Earnings Trigger 'Sell the News' Rout; KOSPI Slumps ~5%, Chips Crater
news.body: Samsung Electronics released preliminary Q2 2026 guidance showing operating profit of 89.4 trillion KRW ($58.7B) — a 19-fold year-on-year surge beating consensus of ~84–87 trillion KRW — but revenue of 171 trillion KRW missed estimates of ~172–174 trillion KRW. Despite the record profit, Samsung shares plunged 7.7% as foreign investors executed 'sell the news' profit-taking, with SK Hynix down 6.7%. The KOSPI fell as much as 8% intraday, closing 4.9% lower at 7,656, with analysts at Mirae Asset citing foreign portfolio rebalancing. Full divisional results are due July 30.

news.headline: Kioxia Plunges Over 11% as Asia Chip Selloff Drags Nikkei 225 Down 2.1%
news.body: Kioxia Holdings, Japan's most valuable listed company, tumbled more than 11% on July 7 — the latest in a string of sharp declines — as the Samsung earnings-driven 'sell the news' dynamic spread across Asia's semiconductor supply chain. Tokyo Electron fell 3.9% and SoftBank shed over 4%, pulling the Nikkei 225 down 2.1% to 68,257. The selloff reflected compounding pressures: AI valuation concerns, profit-taking after extraordinary YTD gains, and the added shock of the Hormuz LNG attack amplifying risk aversion. Taiwan's Taiex lost 2.3% and the Hang Seng declined 0.7%.

news.headline: SK Hynix Sets $29.4B Nasdaq ADR Indicative Price Ahead of Record July 10 Debut
news.body: SK Hynix set its indicative ADR price at KRW 242,500 (~$158.26) per ADR in a revised SEC filing on July 6, ahead of its Nasdaq debut on July 10 under ticker SKHY — targeting ~$29.4B in what would be the largest-ever initial U.S. listing by a foreign company, surpassing Alibaba and Saudi Aramco. The bookbuilding roadshow runs July 6–9, with lead underwriters BofA, Citi, Goldman, and JPMorgan. Proceeds are earmarked for the Yongin fab, Cheongju advanced packaging plant, and EUV lithography equipment. Despite the milestone, SK Hynix shares fell 6.7% on July 7 as broader AI chip sentiment deteriorated.

news.headline: Qatari LNG Tanker Al Rekayyat Struck by Projectile Exiting Strait of Hormuz
news.body: Iran's IRGC allegedly fired missiles at two commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz overnight July 6-7, striking the Nakilat-owned LNG carrier Al Rekayyat ~8 nautical miles east of Limah, Oman, causing a fire and MAYDAY call with no reported casualties. A second Qatari LNG tanker, Al Areesh, reversed course upon news of the attack. European natural gas prices jumped as much as 4.5% on the news in early Asian trade, while Brent crude ticked higher, as the strike directly threatens Qatar's LNG export revival from Ras Laffan. The incident tests the durability of the interim US-Iran ceasefire agreement and raises serious questions about safe transit on the US-endorsed Omani corridor.

news.headline: Gold Steadies at $4,150 as FOMC Minutes Awaited; JPMorgan Caps Q3 Outlook at $4,300
news.body: Gold consolidated around $4,150/oz on July 7 after retreating from two-week highs on USD strength, with markets awaiting Wednesday's Fed June meeting minutes for fresh rate-path signals. The June NFP miss — 57,000 vs. 110,000 forecast — pared September rate-hike odds to ~50% via CME FedWatch, providing gold with a floor despite headwinds from higher real yields and a recovering Hormuz situation that has eased the geopolitical risk premium. JPMorgan noted in a Friday report that demand from key sectors may not be as strong as expected, capping its Q3 gold outlook at $4,300/oz and Q4 at $4,500/oz, while lower oil prices from OPEC+ supply increases helped ease inflationary pressures that had previously weighed on gold.

news.headline: OPEC+ Approves Fifth Consecutive Output Hike of 188K bpd for August
news.body: Seven OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman — agreed on July 5 to raise collective output by 188,000 barrels per day from August, the fifth straight monthly increase and part of a cumulative ~940,000 bpd unwinding since the US-Iran war began. Brent crude held below $72/bbl heading into Monday, near its lowest since late February, as recovering Strait of Hormuz flows and the steady quota restoration reinforced a supply-glut narrative; the IEA projects a 2026 surplus of ~3.84 million bpd. Analysts at Sparta Commodities described the quotas as "essentially meaningless" in the short term given that actual physical barrels have been constrained by the Hormuz blockade, with the real price driver being the pace of transit normalization.

news.headline: Saudi Aramco Slashes August Arab Light OSP for Asia by $11/bbl — Biggest Cut in 26 Years
news.body: Saudi Aramco set its August official selling price for Arab Light crude to Asian buyers at a $1.50 discount to the Oman/Dubai benchmark, an $11/barrel reduction that is the largest single-month OSP cut since at least 2000 and the first time the grade has been sold at a discount since the 2020 price war. The cut, which exceeded a Bloomberg survey median of ~$5/bbl, signals intensifying competition for Asian market share as Hormuz flows recover and Iranian crude re-enters the market, pressuring competing exporters including Russia and US shale producers. Aramco's Q1 2026 free cash flow of $18.6bn already fell short of its $21.89bn quarterly dividend obligation, highlighting the fiscal strain from simultaneous volume and price concessions.

news.headline: Silver Surges ~6% Weekly on NFP Miss, Easing Fed Hike Bets; Deficit Narrative Intact
news.body: Silver futures rallied nearly 6% in the week ending July 4-6, with spot prices touching above $62/oz — their highest since June 23 — after June US nonfarm payrolls came in at just 57,000, roughly half the consensus forecast of 110,000-115,000, sharply reducing expectations for a September Fed rate hike from ~67% to ~50%. Silver opened at $62.92 on July 6 before pulling back modestly, with the Silver Institute confirming 2026 marks a sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit at a 46.3 million troy oz shortfall, underpinning the macro-driven move. Lower rate-hike probability reduced the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding metals, while a weakening USD delivered its largest weekly decline since April, amplifying commodity gains.
